standard_prerequisites.name: Normalised and associated complexes
standard_prerequisites.statement: For a simplicial object U, the associated chain complex s(U) with s(U)_n = U_n and differential the alternating sum of the face maps, and the normalised complex N(U) whose n-th term is the quotient of U_n by the degenerate simplices.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the source and target of the canonical map (source lines 3999-4001).

standard_prerequisites.name: Vanishing of the faces on the normalised subobject
standard_prerequisites.statement: For i smaller than n the face map d^n_i vanishes on the kernel of the sum of the degeneracy maps, i.e. on the normalised subobject.
standard_prerequisites.use: It kills all but the last term of the alternating sum (source lines 4006-4008).

standard_prerequisites.name: The boundary map of the normalised complex
standard_prerequisites.statement: The differential of N(U) is induced by the last face map d^n_n, up to the standard sign.
standard_prerequisites.use: It identifies the surviving term with the boundary map (source lines 4008-4009).

core_obligations: Write the differentials: express the differential of s(U)_n as the alternating sum of the face maps (source lines 4005-4006).
Use the vanishing: observe that the terms with i smaller than n vanish on N(U_n) (source lines 4006-4008).
Identify the survivor: recognise the restriction of the remaining term as the boundary map of N(U), which proves the compatibility with differentials (source lines 4008-4009).

proof_roadmap.step: Write the differential of s(U) as the alternating sum of the face maps.
Kill the terms vanishing on N(U) and identify the last one with the boundary map.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own lemma lemma-map-associated-complexes at source lines 3996-4002: for a simplicial object U of an abelian category the canonical maps N(U_n) to U_n assemble into a morphism of complexes N(U) to s(U). The proof at source lines 4004-4010 is a direct computation with the differentials: on s(U)_n the differential is the alternating sum of the face maps, the face maps with i smaller than n vanish on the normalised subobject, and what remains is exactly the boundary map of N(U) by definition. It is short; the substance is the observation that all but one term of the alternating sum dies on N, which is the definitional reason the two differentials agree.
